title: Deadly Explosion Rocks Europe's Largest Port in Rotterdam, One Killed
excerpt: A blast at a petroleum storage facility at the Port of Rotterdam killed one person and injured several others during maintenance work, prompting emergency response across the sprawling industrial complex.
body:
• One person was killed and several others injured in an explosion at a petroleum storage facility at Rotterdam port on Thursday
  • The blast occurred at a Gunvor Energy storage tank during maintenance work around 11:30 a.m. local time
  • Police said there was no immediate sign of sabotage, but all scenarios remain under investigation
  • ExxonMobil separately shut its 191,000-barrel-per-day Rotterdam refinery due to a power outage, though officials said the two incidents were unrelated

Blast During Maintenance Work

A blast at a storage facility for petroleum products at the Netherlands' Rotterdam port killed one person and wounded several others on Thursday, officials said. The cause of the explosion remains unknown and is under investigation.

A spokesperson for Gunvor, a major energy commodities trading company, said an "incident" occurred during maintenance work on a storage tank at the Europoort section of the port. A police spokesperson said there was no immediate sign of sabotage, but all possible scenarios were being examined, according to Reuters.

The explosion occurred around 11:30 a.m. local time (0930 GMT) on the Moezelweg in Europoort, a heavily industrialized petrochemical section of the port, according to police. Six ambulances, a trauma helicopter, and fire crews rushed to the scene, The Sun reported.

Europe's Largest Port

Rotterdam is Europe's largest port and the 11th busiest in the world by cargo tonnage. The sprawling facility comprises oil refineries, liquefied natural gas terminals, and multiple petrochemical facilities. Shell, ExxonMobil, BP, and Gunvor Energy are among the major companies operating there.

"An explosion took place on the Moezelweg around 11:30 a.m.," a police statement read. "We are investigating how this happened. A crime scene has been established and the labor inspectorate is also arriving on site. Several people were injured in the explosion and one person has died."

Pictures circulated on social media showed visible traces of the explosion on a storage tank. It has been suggested that something may have gone wrong during the disconnection of pipelines, though this has not been confirmed.

Separate Power Outage Disrupts Refinery

Adding to the disruption, ExxonMobil shut all units at its 191,000-barrel-per-day Rotterdam refinery due to a separate power outage, consultancy Wood Mackenzie said in an alert to clients seen by Reuters. The power outage had triggered a Grip 2 emergency — the second level of the Netherlands' crisis management protocol — at a refinery on Botlekweg about two hours before the explosion.

Rotterdam Port officials said there was no connection between the blast and the power outage. ExxonMobil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Shell said its operations at the port were unaffected by the blast. A Rotterdam Port spokesperson confirmed that LNG terminals were also not affected.

Investigation Underway

Gunvor said it was cooperating with local authorities. The labor inspectorate has arrived on site alongside police investigators.

The incident comes at a time of heightened attention to energy infrastructure security in Europe. While authorities stressed there was no immediate indication of intentional action, the location of the blast at one of the continent's most critical energy hubs underscores the potential vulnerabilities of industrial facilities.
nri_angle: Rotterdam port is a critical node in global energy supply chains, and disruptions there can ripple through fuel and commodity prices that affect Indian consumers and businesses worldwide.
